title: Carbon-Accountable Performance Contracting in Desalination Public–Private Partnerships: Investment Incentives, Controllability, and Assurance Costs
content: Carbon incentives in seawater reverse-osmosis (SWRO) public–private partnerships can reward measured changes that are not controlled by the operator. This paper tests a carbon-accountable performance contract (CACPC) against an otherwise matched unadjusted carbon-reward contract (C3). We implement the numerical comparison with a single uncertainty deduction, exclude an unsupported private reputational benefit for undetected false reporting, conserve payment transfers, and separate observable resource–carbon outcomes from a retrospective attribution-error diagnostic. The illustrative SWRO plant and all tariffs, costs, attribution shares and reporting behaviors are synthetic. The numerical experiment contains 135 distinct investment-input configurations; a 675-row attribution diagnostic includes deliberately repeated configurations and is not an empirical sample. Under the specified positive incremental assurance cost, CACPC never lowers the primary resource-plus-carbon score in the 675-row diagnostic, although a latent-truth retrospective score sometimes favors it. The result is a conditional methodological finding: attribution-adjusted payments may improve retrospective credit alignment, but such improvements do not establish social value or real emissions savings without credible identification, calibrated verification cost and prospectively available information.
